checks.finding: The finite exceptional set bounds all outside ellipse radii by a < R. Its strict nondominant subset admits a common r < R with a <= r. The union of those two complements is the complement of the maximal affine head.
The phase-attaining node cannot lie outside the exceptional set. Filtering equality retains it; every excluded node has affine norm <= r < R.
A fiber coefficient equals its natural cardinality cast to C times the node. Image membership makes the cardinality positive; D.node_ne_zero prevents cancellation to zero.
The chosen phase differs from one, so the affine map is injective. Finset.image removes equal node values, and equivFin provides an injective enumeration.
Pinned equivFin, Fintype.sum_equiv, Finset.sum_finset_coe, and sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to orientations match the proof. Coercions and local lets are definitionally aligned.
The finite exponential sum is exactly the grouped finite head. The supplied generating split gives this head plus the full subtype-complement remainder, without dropping any indices.
The constructed r satisfies 1 <= r < R. The existing total norm mass bounds the complement uniformly by mass * r^N, matching DominantTailData fields.
